items.name: ponytail
items.author: DietrichGebert
items.why: The smallest change that finishes the job. Leave validation, error handling, security, and accessibility in place.

items.name: ponytail-review
items.author: DietrichGebert
items.why: Read it like someone who gets paged.

items.name: ponytail-audit
items.author: DietrichGebert
items.why: That same pass, over every file.

items.name: ponytail-debt
items.author: DietrichGebert
items.when: Shortcuts you meant to come back to

items.name: diagnosing-bugs
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Something is broken, throwing, failing, or slow — a hard bug
items.why: Build a tight feedback loop first, then localize, reduce, fix, and guard.

items.name: premortem
items.author: GeorgeT
items.when: A change that touches data, money, jobs, or what a person sees
items.why: Name where it can break before you write. A small change gets a short answer.

items.name: grill-me
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: They asked to grill a plan or design, or the ask is underspecified
items.why: Interview until every branch of the design tree is resolved. Uses grilling.

items.name: grilling
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: Stress-testing a plan, decision, or idea
items.why: The interview primitive behind grill-me. Relentless questions until branches are closed.

items.name: design-reference-hunt
items.author: Long Beard
items.when: No official look, or they asked to hunt / define direction / find references
items.why: Does not code the page. Ask once for a Figma file. Whole look writes `.design/board.md` and, after they pick a primary, `.design/moodboard.html` from that board. A later pass writes `.design/hunts/<slug>/` and does not replace the moodboard. Open the moodboard, say the direction in chat, then ask to write or update `DESIGN.md` via design-md as its own message — once more, first, if they move on without answering — only on yes. Direction-only stops there. Build only if they also asked to build.

items.name: design-taste-frontend
items.author: Leonxlnx
items.when: They asked to build or code a page or screen
items.why: Do not deal this skill’s references, and do not run draw. Prefer `DESIGN.md` when it exists; else wait for `.design/board.md` and build from those cards. Direction-only or hunt-only is not this skill. The control a card describes is the control. Do not add a filled button the card does not show. Inspect still.

items.name: animate
items.author: emilkowalski
items.when: They asked to animate a control or a transition
items.why: A page design-taste-frontend is building keeps that skill’s motion. Decide this one move, then build it.

items.name: figma-design-to-code
items.author: Figma
items.why: A designer handed it over. Needs the Figma connection. Reuse this project's components.

items.name: image-to-code
items.author: Leonxlnx
items.why: Build the page from that picture.

items.name: security-audit
items.author: Cloudflare
items.when: A security review you asked for
items.why: Look for a broken trust boundary. The full audit runs only when you ask for an audit or a pen-test.

items.name: web-design-guidelines
items.author: Vercel
items.when: A UI review you asked for

items.name: jury
items.author: juliobsz
items.when: They asked to jury, score, judge, or roast the design (or a live URL / local build)
items.why: Blind evidence scorecard. Do not redesign. Fixes stay on the board, DESIGN.md, or Figma. Do not run after every build unless they asked.

items.name: handoff
items.author: Matt Pocock
items.when: They asked to hand off to another agent or session
items.why: Compact the conversation into a handoff document another agent can pick up.

items.name: design-md
items.author: Long Beard
items.when: The look of this project, or they confirmed writing or updating DESIGN.md
items.why: Follow DESIGN.md when it exists. Write or update it from the board or a hunt note only when they confirm — expand colour, type, control, layout principles, leave. Do not invent. Missing file plus design or define direction is hunt first.
